details: Oil prices have fallen, influenced by US President Donald Trump's decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, though a final decision is pending. This comes as Iran reported another tanker hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, adding to geopolitical tensions. Despite this, falling oil prices offered some support to bonds and Wall Street stock futures.
title: Oil Prices Fall Amid Geopolitical Events; Iran Tanker Incident Reported

details: France experienced significant rioting over the weekend, among the worst in years. This civil unrest is occurring at a time of political transition and fiscal challenges in the country, leading to the euro weakening against the dollar. The widespread protests have contributed to a lower open for European stock futures.
title: Widespread Rioting in France Weighs on European Sentiment

details: The chair of the IMF's International Monetary and Financial Committee stated on October 17th that the global economy remains resilient but faces pressures from ongoing conflicts, energy prices, and high public debt. Governments have been urged to rebuild fiscal buffers to withstand future economic shocks.
title: IMF Warns on Global Economic Resilience Amid Conflicts, Debt

details: MSCI announced new screening criteria on October 15th for "non-operating companies," potentially leading to the exclusion of firms with significant cryptocurrency treasuries, such as Strategy and Metaplanet, from their global indices. This change, effective after the November review, focuses on operational substance and could trigger fund outflows and impact future financing for affected companies.
title: MSCI to Exclude Crypto Treasury Firms from Indices

details: The Bank of Russia confirmed a hard deadline of July 1, 2027, to permanently outlaw direct peer-to-peer cryptocurrency trading between individual citizens. Updated guidance published on October 12th clarifies this federal law.
title: Russia Sets Hard Deadline to Outlaw P2P Crypto Trades

details: Circle Internet Group is aggressively expanding its USDC stablecoin into 40 new emerging markets across Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East. This move aims to capture surging global demand for stablecoins for commercial payments and cross-border money transfers, putting Circle in direct competition with traditional banks.
title: Circle Expands USDC Stablecoin into 40 Emerging Markets
